subject: The Papyrus · The waterway that lost 61% in a single year
html:
One chokepoint, one budget-sized swing

The Suez Canal is one of Egypt's crown assets — a 164 km cut that carries a meaningful slice of all seaborne world trade. In the fiscal year ending June 2023 it earned a record ~$9.4bn. The very next calendar year, 2024, it took in about $3.99bn. That is a 61% collapse in twelve months. (Source: Suez Canal Authority.)

What happened

From November 2023, attacks on Red Sea shipping pushed vessels to reroute the long way around Africa. Canal traffic fell by roughly half, and container ships — the high-value cargo — by about 90%. Only around 13,213 vessels transited in 2024. A single waterway had just moved a national budget. (Sources: Suez Canal Authority; Egypt Today.)

A data-literacy footnote worth keeping

The same canal shows up as $9.4bn for FY2022/23 and $10.25bn for calendar-year 2023. That is not an error — it is two different accounting windows over an overlapping period. EgyBI's suez_canal_revenue table labels each row as fiscal or calendar year precisely so you never compare the wrong two numbers. Getting that right is the job.

The whole series from 2016 to 2024 sits in that table: watch the line climb to a record, then fall off a cliff.
